ink.purpose: Primary text, and the fill for the ACCEPTED plate and the ink button. One warm black.

ink-soft.purpose: Secondary text and button hover borders.

ink-faint.purpose: Metadata, field labels, column heads, and the COMPLETED plate text.

mark.purpose: Shapes that are never words: the switch knob and the order-trail chevron's border. Below the text threshold by design — never reuse it for type.

mark-quiet.purpose: The quietest mark in the system, used once: the counter-sale source dot. Permitted only because the word COUNTER sits beside it.

desk.purpose: The counter ground behind every sheet; also the page background gradient's lower stop and the fill behind a quantity chip.

stock.purpose: The near-white every ticket, input, button and sheet is printed on. The system's paper.

stock-tray.purpose: One step down from stock. Lane bodies and the torn-stub corner gradient — and the ground the NEW tray's jute tint is mixed into.

stock-ledger.purpose: The bill sheet, a hair warmer than tray stock so an invoice reads as its own kind of paper.

rule.purpose: 16% ink. A section divider or a panel head rule.

rule-mid.purpose: 30% ink. A container, lane or button border, and the dashed accepted sub-band. Never an interactive control's boundary — that takes --control-edge, which clears the 3:1 non-text floor this measures 2.00:1 below.

rule-hair.purpose: 8% ink. A table row divider. The faintest line in the system.

control-edge.purpose: The boundary of a control — every .input, select.input and the .switch track. A rule divides, an edge locates: a control's boundary has to be findable, and WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1 for a shape that carries meaning without words. Measures 6.41:1 on --stock and 5.24:1 on --desk, where --rule-mid at 30% measures 2.00:1 and 1.96:1.

rail.purpose: The one dark surface: the machined top rail, sticky at --rail-h.

rail-line.purpose: A 10% white hairline: the border of the rail's buttons and pills.

rail-ink.purpose: Primary text on iron. Paper ink cannot sit on the dark ground.

rail-ghost.purpose: Inactive tabs, sub-labels and counts on iron.

jute.purpose: The one accent, and the seal. Primary button, NEW plate, current-tab underline, NEW lane count, arrival toast, row-hover underline — and the 11% tint mixed into tray stock to mark the NEW tray as the one that needs work.

jute-deep.purpose: Jute pressed further: the seal button's border, the NEW plate's inner ring, the ON switch, and the border of the tinted NEW tray.

jute-wash.purpose: Jute thinned to a ground: notes, demo tags, ON switch track, fresh-ticket glow, default toast.

verdigris.purpose: PREPARING. The PREPARING plate, the PREPARING lane count, the meter fill.

verdigris-wash.purpose: The PREPARING ground at low emphasis: the calm note strip, the calm toast.

ledger.purpose: READY. The READY plate, the READY lane count, the online LED.

india.purpose: Money and refusal. Every ticket total and every row total, the CANCELLED plate, the grand-total rule, the danger button.

india-wash.purpose: Red thinned to a ground: the warning note strip, the alert toast, the danger hover.

graphite.purpose: COMPLETED, and the only tray ink with no wash. A terminal state gets a neutral, not a fifth bright hue.

on-jute.purpose: Text set on a filled jute plate or the seal button. Named for its ground so the two retint together.

on-jute-deep.purpose: Text on the NEW lane-count block, the darkest of the on-jute steps so a small figure holds on gold.

on-graphite.purpose: The tally strip's micro labels on ink; also the value that reads on a graphite lane count.

jute-edge.purpose: The seal button's hover border: jute pressed past its own deep step.

fig-jute.purpose: The lightened jute a seal button hovers to, and the last --fig-* token. The tally strip no longer tints its figures: the strip carries the day's arithmetic, which has no status. --fig-verdigris and --fig-ledger were deleted with the strip cells that used them; a '--fig-<ink>' family with one member is a name waiting to drift.

alert.purpose: The full-bleed offline band under the tally strip.

alert-ink.purpose: Body text on the india-wash note strip.

alert-deep.purpose: Text on a ticket's warning flag, where the ground is narrower and the text needs the contrast.

alert-led.purpose: The offline band's LED; near-white so it survives on a saturated red band.

note-ink.purpose: Text on a ticket's jute-wash note flag.

note-deep.purpose: Text on a jute-wash tag, one step off the note flag for the smaller surface.

calm-ink.purpose: Text on the verdigris-wash note strip.

whatsapp.purpose: The source dot on an incoming ticket, and nothing else in the product.

ink-hover.purpose: The ink button's hover: ink, warmed a step toward hover rather than darkened.

desk-lit.purpose: The page background gradient's upper stop, a step lighter than the desk it sits on.

rail-grain.purpose: 2.2% white. The brushed-metal grain repeating 1px every 3px on the iron rail.

rail-wash.purpose: 5% white. A tab's hover ground and the rail's top light.

rail-soft.purpose: 6% white. The ground of the rail's metal fittings and its machined top highlight.

rail-hair.purpose: 11% white. The tally strip's cell dividers.

rail-lift.purpose: 12% white. The hover ground of an icon button or the demo button.

edge-hair.purpose: 22% black. The stamp plate's mottle dot layer and the finest edge on dark.

edge-soft.purpose: 30% black. The offline band's top rule.

edge.purpose: 40% black. The tally strip's rules against the ink ground.

edge-deep.purpose: 50% black. The rail's machined bottom inset edge.

ink-alpha.purpose: 16% black. The stamp plate's inner bleed.

ink-alpha-w.purpose: 16% white. The second, offset dot layer of the stamp plate's mottle.

shade-deep.purpose: 28% of the paper ink. The sticky footer bars' scroll-cue.

scrim.purpose: 42% of the paper ink. The wash behind the drawer and the bill sheet.

print-ink.purpose: A thermal head draws one black on white. Never retinted toward the screen palette.

print-ground.purpose: The receipt's paper. A device colour, not a stock.

mask-solid.purpose: The rail-nav fade mask's key. A mask must be fully opaque or it does not mask, so this cannot be a palette ink.

display.purpose: Stencil 700 at var(--t-figure) (1.5rem). The day band on Bills and the bill-sheet grand total. The largest type in the product is a number.

headline.purpose: Stencil 700 uppercase at var(--t-screen), 0.14em. Screen titles on Bills, Products, Customers and Settings, the bill sheet bar, panel headers. The order board is the exception: .board-title is --t-lead because it shares a line with a 13px sentence.

lot-number.purpose: Stencil 700 at var(--t-lot) (1.1875rem) with a 0.34em gutter per space. The identity of every ticket; animates in character by character at 26ms steps.

total.purpose: Stencil 700 at var(--t-total), tabular. The full card's foot figure and the tally strip's figures, each with its rupee set separately in Archivo. A row's total steps down to --t-mark, and a row's lot number to --t-lead, because a claimed ticket is scanned rather than read.

title.purpose: Stencil 400 at var(--t-name) (0.9375rem). Customer and shop names on the full card, the drawer and the bill sheet. In a row the name is Archivo at the same size — it is the one string on a row that must never truncate.

body.purpose: Archivo 400 at the document default of 15px/1.5. Item names, notes, empty-state prose.

copy.purpose: Archivo at var(--t-lead) (0.875rem). Prose blocks, inputs, fact lists, note text, and the board's one-sentence summary, which is prose rather than body copy.

control.purpose: Archivo 600 at var(--t-body) (0.8125rem), the workhorse. Buttons, inputs, table cells, ticket lines.

label.purpose: Archivo 700 at var(--micro) (0.6875rem), uppercase, 0.14em-0.16em. A hard floor for functional text: this screen is read at arm's length under bad light. Nothing functional goes below it, and a row's action label sits exactly on it.

mono.purpose: Platform monospace at 0.8125em, -0.01em, tabular numerals — the ramp's one deliberately em-relative step, so a figure shrinks with whatever it sits inside. Phone numbers, IDs, and every money column including the receipt.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Paper resting on the desk. A 1px hard contact line plus a 4px diffuse. Tickets and sheet cards only.

shadows.name: lift-up
shadows.purpose: Paper picked up off the desk: drawer, bill sheet, connector sheet, toast, alerting ticket.

shadows.name: rail-edge
shadows.purpose: The machined bottom edge (--edge-deep) and top highlight (--rail-soft) of the iron rail. A lit metal edge, not a card. The brushed grain over it is a 1px hairline repeating every 3px at --rail-grain — a material, kept over the sweep's repeating-stripes finding.

shadows.name: footer-cue
shadows.purpose: Lets scrolling content pass under a sticky footer bar (drawer foot, bill sheet foot).

shadows.name: focus
shadows.purpose: The single focus ring for the whole product: a stock gap so an india ring reads on any ground.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Button background, border and colour transitions.

motion.name: nav
motion.purpose: Tab colour, inset underline and ground.

motion.name: switch
motion.purpose: The toggle knob's slide and colour.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Button :active translateY(1px). The button physically presses.

motion.name: stamp-press
motion.purpose: The rubber stamp falls, contacts hard at 38%, settles. The overshoot stays; the elastic tail does not.

motion.name: ticket-in
motion.purpose: A new lot ticket arriving on the desk.

motion.name: split-flap
motion.purpose: The lot number flipping in, character by character.

motion.name: perf-glow
motion.purpose: The punched perforation briefly glowing jute wash on arrival.

motion.name: sync-pulse
motion.purpose: The only loop in the system: the connection LED while syncing.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Collapses every animation and transition globally in tokens.css.

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.purpose: Board 4 -> 2 columns. The tally stays at three cells; its labels do not clip at any width down to 720px.

breakpoints.name: rail-wrap
breakpoints.purpose: The rail wraps to two rows so no tab is ever off-canvas, and the board's one sentence takes its own full-width line under the title; 2/3-col grids and the bill sheet collapse to one.

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.purpose: Board to 1 column; the tally becomes a stack of three label-left/figure-right bands rather than three columns, because three labels side by side clip at 390px; drawer to 100vw.

breakpoints.name: bill-foot
breakpoints.purpose: The bill sheet footer bar stacks and stretches.

components.name: Seal Button
components.description: The primary action and the only filled-jute control. Always ends in a chevron, because a seal is a press that moves the ticket forward.

components.name: Ink Button
components.description: The dark commitment, used on the ink bar of the bill sheet.

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Default for secondary actions. Hover fills with stock so the button gains weight only under the pointer.

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: Never a filled red. Transparent with an india hairline; the hover fills with india wash.

components.name: Stamp Plate
components.description: Status as a filled, inked plate rotated -1.5deg with a multiply-blended ink mottle and an inner bleed — never a dot, never a faint tint, and always carrying its word. NEW/ACCEPTED/PREPARING/READY are filled; COMPLETED and CANCELLED are outlined, because a state that is no longer in play should not spend an ink.

components.name: Lot Ticket
components.description: The signature component at its full density, and the only status that gets it: NEW, where accepting the order means reading it. On the card only the customer name is a button; the lot number is a plain stencil span, a recorded gap rather than a decision. A row makes both of them controls. Past NEW the same ticket prints as the two-line Ticket Row — a ticket needs reading only while nobody has claimed it, and scanning after that.

components.name: Ticket Row
components.description: The second density, for every status past NEW: 77px instead of 341px, seven rows to a tray instead of one and a half. Line one is identity and money, line two is the customer and the action. The lot number and the name are the two buttons that open the order — there is no View order button, because in a row it would cost more room than the name it protects. A row's height is fixed by its two lines, so a third fact is a layout change, not an addition. The perforation band is the card's 8px geometry, not a shortened copy of it: the tear hairline sits at 7px inside the band, so a 6px band paints the hairline outside its own box and the row shows no tear line at all. The lot number ellipsizes rather than spilling — latent for SAM-NNNNN, but the connector mints whatever order_id the cloud sends.

components.name: Lane Count Block
components.description: Region-scale colour: a filled 1.5rem block carrying the tray's ticket count, tinted by tray ink. A zero count hides entirely. The NEW tray behind it is the tinted one — jute mixed into tray stock — so the tray that needs work is identifiable before anything in it is read. Nothing else may take that tint.

components.name: Board Say
components.description: The one plain-English sentence beside the screen title. The board must explain itself before it is read, and this is the only line that does. It is prose, so it takes Archivo and not the stencil — and it is the one place on the board where a figure is deliberately restated in words. A sentence the screen speaks is a claim: settled today filters on createdAt >= todayStart, and the WhatsApp clause counts only source === 'whatsapp', with counter-sourced tickets claimed in their own clause — otherwise the prose drifts away from the figures printed beside it.

components.name: Tally Cell
components.description: One of three cells on the ink strip, carrying the day's arithmetic and nothing the board already shows: Today's bills, Today's sales, Bills via WhatsApp. The strip used to carry six cells printing the queue counts the tabs and tray heads already print, so 4/3/2 appeared three times each. The figures are stock, not tinted — there is no status on the strip any more. The sales figure sets its rupee separately from the number and one step down at 0.66em, like every other total in the product; writing it as one text node sets the sign at the figure's full weight and size and breaks the pattern.

components.name: Rail Tab
components.description: Section navigation on the iron rail. The current tab is underlined in jute, never a filled pill. Counts are stencil chips that invert when hot and vanish at zero.

components.name: Text Field
components.description: Tabular numerals, a 1.5px control-edge border — an alpha rule measures 2:1 and fails the 3:1 floor a boundary has to clear — and a micro uppercase field label. Focus shifts the border to ink and takes the product focus ring.

components.name: Switch
components.description: A machined toggle: a desk track with a --mark knob that slides in jute-deep onto a jute-wash track when on. Its boundary takes --control-edge rather than a rule, because a track's edge is what makes it findable. The knob is a shape, so it wears a mark rather than a lightened ink.

components.name: Note Flag
components.description: A ticket note or a warning. The wash is the signal, with a 1px ink ring instead of a heavier border.

components.name: CSS-Drawn Icons
components.description: Every icon in this system is drawn from borders, gradients and clip-paths — including the warning triangle, whose bar is knocked out in the flag's own ground so it reads on red stock. No icon font, no glyph character, no , no fetched SVG.

narrative.overview:
This is a ticket printer's desk at the wholesale mandi, not a task manager. An incoming WhatsApp order is a numbered lot ticket already printed on white stock — customer, lines, GST slab, total — and the only thing the operator ever does to it is press a rubber stamp. That premise decides everything else: the screen is four trays on a counter, not four columns of cards; the rails and dividers are torn paper edges and hairline rules, with a single small contact shadow kept for paper lying on the counter or lifted off it; and the loudest thing on any surface is a lot number wearing a stencil face, because on a real ticket the number is what you read.

The material is drawn, not imported. Ticket edges are punched with a repeating radial-gradient that leaves a tear hairline under the notches. The bottom-right corner of every ticket is torn off with a single 315deg gradient. Stamp plates carry an ink mottle — two multiply-blended dot layers over an inner bleed — so the status colour looks pressed rather than filled. The rail wears a brushed grain from a 1px hairline every 3px at 2.2% white. Every mark in the product is drawn the same way — the chevron, the speaker cone, the printer, the warning triangle. None of this is decoration for its own sake: each device is the cheapest CSS that produces the material it names, and the world refuses anything it cannot justify that way.

It is a dense screen. The operator is standing at a fixed terminal, reading at arm's length under bad light, and every tap costs a stamp. So the build is quiet by default and loud only where the operator must act: colour commits at **region scale** — a filled lane-count block, a filled stamp plate, the ink tally strip — and never as scattered accents. Nothing functional goes below `--micro` (0.6875rem / 11px), a floor that exists because the room is bright and the reader is not.

Density is a decision, not a constant. A ticket needs **reading** only while nobody has claimed it; after that it needs **scanning**. So the board runs two densities — a full card in the NEW tray, a two-line row everywhere else — and the whole layout is budgeted around that. On the target viewport (1366×768) the chrome before the first ticket is 199px, a live card is 283px, and a row is 77px, which is what turns a tray from one and a half visible tickets into seven.
keyCharacteristics: Paper-and-ink neutrals plus exactly one accent (jute gold); a five-ink stamp tray for state.
Two ticket densities on one board: the full card where a decision is made, a two-line row everywhere past it.
Stencil (Stardos Stencil) for every number that must be read at a glance; Archivo for everything else.
Status is a filled, rotated, mottled stamp plate with a text label — never a dot, never a tint.
Hairline rules and drawn material; one small contact shadow, reserved for paper at rest or lifted.
One perforation geometry at two densities: an 8px band, a 1px tear hairline at 7px, notches on a 9px period. A height change to one density is a regression in the other.
The rupee sign always sets separately from the figure, one step down, never inside the numeral.
A sentence the screen speaks is a claim, and gets the same filtering as the numbers it summarises.
Every size, radius and colour is a named token in `tokens.css`; the sweep found nothing left as a literal.
Integer paise and `en-IN` grouping on every rupee figure, in every surface including the receipt.
A number appears once on a surface; the strip carries only what the board does not already show.

dos: **Do** press a status change as a filled stamp plate with a text label, and let `.is-stamped` play.
**Do** commit colour at region scale — a filled plate, a filled count block, the tally strip.
**Do** keep every rupee figure in integer paise and format it with `en-IN` grouping; keep tabular numerals on every money column.
**Do** separate layers with a hairline rule, `--lift` for paper at rest, or `--lift-up` for paper picked up.
**Do** keep functional text at or above `--micro` (0.6875rem / 11px), and take every other size from the ramp (`--t-label` → `--t-figure`) rather than writing one out.
**Do** draw an icon in CSS from borders, gradients or clip-paths, the way `.chev`, `.icon-mute`, `.icon-print` and `.warn-glyph` already are.

**Do** name a colour that sits on a stamp ink `--on-<that ink>`, and reach for an existing token before writing a literal. Where an alpha wash is needed off a tray ink, write `color-mix(in oklch, var(--india) 40%, transparent)` so the tray stays the source.

**Do** keep `--print-ink`, `--print-ground` and `--mask-solid` as device colours when you touch the receipt, set the tray's base with `--tray-*-type`, and size every line inside `#receipt` in `em` against that base so the receipt scales with the tray.
**Do** let the stencil stack fall through to Archivo for `₹`; that is the shipped result.
**Do** set the rupee sign separately from the figure and one step down, in every money run — `'₹' + figure`, never `SV.money()` as one text node.
**Do** write a sentence's numbers with the same predicates as the figures it summarises, and drop a clause rather than print a `0`.
**Do** hide a zero count entirely rather than printing a `0`.
**Do** pick the density from the status, not from the available space: the full card in NEW, the two-line row everywhere past it. Past NEW a ticket is claimed and needs scanning, not reading.
**Do** keep the lot number and the customer name as the two controls that open the order, at both densities. Those are the facts an operator recognises a ticket by.
**Do** keep a row's action label whole and shrink the button before the name — `.row-bot .btn` runs `--micro` so that the name never has to.
**Do** print a figure once on a surface. If a second region would show it, cut one of them.
**Do** guard a row's identifiers against the data the connector can actually send: `.row-lot` ellipsizes rather than spilling, and a check that only sees `SAM-NNNNN` has not seen the guard.
**Do** tint the work tray and nothing else; the tint answers "where do I work" and no other question.
**Do** let the board say what it is in one plain sentence, and update it whenever the board renders.
donts: **Don't** render status as a bare dot or a faint tint — the filled plate and its word are the system.

**Don't** add a lighter ink to make something read as muted, and don't reintroduce a fourth step below `--ink-faint`. Muted is a `--mark` or `--mark-quiet` when it is a shape, `--ink-faint` when it is a word, and there is no third option.
**Don't** use a second accent. The tray inks each mean one state; India red is money and refusal only.
**Don't** introduce hex, rgb or hsl alongside the OKLCH source in `tokens.css`.
**Don't** add a shadow that is not `--lift` or `--lift-up`, and don't add a glow or a blur to a resting surface.
**Don't** put functional text below `--micro`, and don't "fix" the stencil stack's missing rupee by removing Archivo from it.
**Don't** set `₹` inside a numeral run, and don't add a second relative font size where a ramp step will do.
**Don't** treat a passing contrast audit as proof about a state no seeded ticket reaches — render the state, then measure it.
**Don't** change the perforation band's height at one density without changing the other, and don't move a tray's hairline to re-tint it. The ink mix is the whole of the tint.
**Don't** border an interactive control with an alpha rule; `--control-edge` is what clears 3:1.
**Don't** hand-write an `oklch` next to a tray ink, and don't invent a sixth ink — extend the tray instead.
**Don't** retint `--print-ink`, `--print-ground` or `--mask-solid` toward the screen palette, and don't reuse a palette ink as a mask key.
**Don't** reach for `--radius-shell` outside the mute speaker cone, or for `--radius-pill` outside the rail's metal fittings.
**Don't** put a dotless kanban, a blue accent, a grey card or a soft elevation shadow on this surface — that is the category default the world exists to refuse.
**Don't** make ACCEPTED its own tray or count. It rides in PREPARING under a dashed sub-band so the tray count, the tab chip and the lane head cannot disagree.
**Don't** re-key an order into a bill. The bill inherits its lines; products are never re-entered.
**Don't** put a third fact on a row. A row's height is fixed by its two lines, so adding one is a layout change: decide what comes off before deciding what goes on.
**Don't** restore a queue count to the tally strip. The tabs and the tray heads already print it, and the strip is for the day's arithmetic only.
**Don't** give a row a "View order" button. The lot number and the name already open the order, and the button would cost more room than the name it protects.
**Don't** truncate the customer name to protect a button, a tag, or a timestamp. Verify row content by measuring `scrollWidth` against `clientWidth`; a screenshot will not show it.
**Don't** let a lot number spill past the ticket onto the tray behind it.
